Anthony Davis is a professional basketball player who has had an impressive career with the New Orleans Pelicans and Los Angeles Lakers. Here are some key points about his career:
Drafted by the New Orleans Hornets (now Pelicans) as the first overall pick in the 2012 NBA draft, he played for them from 2012 to 2019.
In 2019, he was traded to the Los Angeles Lakers along with Brandon Ingram and Lonzo Ball in exchange for Brandon Ingram, Josh Hart, and a future first-round pick.
With the Pelicans, Davis had several standout seasons:
Named NBA All-Star four consecutive times (2017-2020)
Won the 2016 Taco Bell Skills Challenge
Led the league in blocks three straight years (2015-2017)
With the Lakers, he has won an NBA championship with LeBron James and has been named to the All-NBA First Team.
Davis is known for his versatility on both ends of the floor, scoring inside and outside while also being a dominant shot-blocker.
He signed a five-year, $190 million contract extension with the Lakers in 2020.
Davis has represented the USA in international competitions, including the 2014 FIBA World Cup and 2016 Olympics.
In 2023-24, he signed a five-year, $259 million contract extension with the Lakers.
Davis is known for his philanthropy, having donated to build a basketball court at his high school alma mater in Kentucky.
He has been involved in various social media and marketing campaigns, including trademarking his "brow" as part of his brand identity.
Davis has appeared in movies like Barbershop: The Next Cut (2016) and is rumored to be a potential cast member for future basketball-themed films like Space Jam 2 and House Party reboot.
